rationale: Tests recognition of a classic EN known-trap: Battle's sign (post-auricular ecchymosis) indicates base of skull fracture involving the temporal bone, a critical clinical sign in head and neck trauma.
Tests the EN known-trap principle that septal haematoma must be drained urgently to prevent avascular necrosis of the septal cartilage and saddle nose deformity.
Tests understanding of salivary calculus (sialolithiasis) predilection for the submandibular gland due to its anatomy — longer, tortuous Wharton's duct and more mucous secretion.
Tests the EN known-trap: incisional biopsy of a parotid mass is contraindicated because it risks seeding of tumour cells and injury to the facial nerve; FNAC is the safe diagnostic approach.

Tests understanding that the danger space (space 4) communicates directly with the posterior mediastinum, making descending necrotising mediastinitis the most feared and lethal complication of deep neck infection.

Tests application of the principle that airway management in deep neck infection must be proactive and early, and that tracheostomy (not cricothyroidotomy) is preferred when prolonged airway support is anticipated.

Tests understanding that oral hairy leukoplakia is an EN known-trap: it is pathognomonic of HIV-related immunosuppression, cannot be scraped off (distinguishing it from oral candidiasis), and appears on the lateral tongue.

Tests the management principle that antiretroviral therapy (ART) is the cornerstone of managing HIV-related ENT manifestations, and that specific ENT treatments work best when initiated alongside ART.
